claims.text: The initial material is equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr in the cast state.
Controlled oxidation at 500–800 °C in a controlled oxygen environment for 1–10 hours will form a protective oxide layer on cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
The oxide layer formed by controlled oxidation will be dense and adherent.
The dense, adherent oxide layer will prevent further oxidation of the underlying alloy.
The oxide layer will prevent degradation of the underlying alloy.
Controlled oxidation will improve the oxygen resistance of cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
After controlled oxidation, the alloy will maintain a yield strength above 150 MPa at 1000 °C.
After controlled oxidation, the alloy will retain room-temperature tensile ductility above 5%.
Untreated cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
Untreated cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has room-temperature tensile ductility of 8–16%.
The proposed performance boundary is oxidizing service below 1000 °C at strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.

contradictions.description: The stated operating boundary is below 1000 °C, but yield strength is predicted and tested at 1000 °C, which lies outside a strictly interpreted 'below 1000 °C' boundary.

The hypothesis claims no sacrifice of mechanical performance, but the acceptance thresholds permit room-temperature ductility to fall from 8–16% to just above 5% and 1000 °C yield strength to fall from at least 163 MPa to just above 150 MPa.
